title: Lamech
summary: Lamech, son of methuselah, in the line of Seth (Genesis 5).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 4: Ussher, Annals: 874 AM, 3130 BC (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), "Chronological Compendium", p. 1
birth.note: Jones prints only the AM figure here; no BC year is printed for this birth, so year_bc_ad is left null (not inferred).

birth.citation: Gen 5 cumulative begetting ages (father methuselah begat at 187, Gen 5:25)
Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §20 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §4 "The Chronology of Genesis 4 & 5" (year list)

birth.date: 874 AM (birth year printed at the start of the lamech bar)
birth.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 1, chart "A.M. Chronology (Anno Mundi “Year of the World”) Genesis 5, 11:10"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 874.

birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 781b
birth.note: Year cell "1557 875". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 777 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints. His table also prints the death at World 1651. 875 + 777 is not 1651. Both figures are left as printed.

birth.date: Hebrew table, “Lamech”: began his life in the year of the world 874
birth.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book I, p. 44 (facsimile PDF p. 134)
birth.note: Hebrew table on p. 44, the row headed “Lamech”. The same row prints: had his son in year 182 of his life; lived 595 years after that birth; lived in all 777 years. Shuckford introduces the table as the computations of Moses according to our Hebrew Bibles.

birth.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxii

death.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

death.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §32 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

death.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 1651.

death.note: Year cell "2333 1651". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682.
